create_stacking_fault_workflow(atoms, formula=None, info='Calculated', optimizer='FIRE', working_dir=None)

Create a stacking-fault workflow that reuses this workflow calculator.

Parameters:

  • atoms – Reference structure used to build the faulted slab.

  • formula (str | None) – Optional chemical formula label used in output filenames.

  • info (str) – Short label written into summary files and plot legends.

  • optimizer (str) – Geometry optimizer label passed to the stacking-fault workflow.

  • working_dir (str | None) – Optional directory for stacking-fault outputs. When omitted, self.working_dir is reused.

Returns:

Workflow instance sharing this calculator.

Return type:

StackingFaultWorkflow

Create a traction-separation workflow that reuses this workflow calculator.

Parameters:

  • atoms – Reference bulk or slab structure.

  • surface_index – Optional surface Miller index such as (1, 0, 0).

  • repeat – Supercell repetition counts along the slab directions.

  • working_dir (str | None) – Optional directory for traction-separation outputs. When omitted, self.working_dir is reused.

  • optimizer (str) – Geometry optimizer label passed to the TS workflow.

Returns:

Workflow instance sharing this calculator.

Return type:

TractionSeparationWorkflow

calculate_phonon_dispersion(structure, special_points=None, labels_path=None, formula=None, info=None, supercell_matrix=None, primitive_matrix='auto')

Calculate and plot the phonon dispersion relation.

Parameters:

  • structure – Structure used for the phonon calculation.

  • special_points (dict[str, tuple[float, float, float]] | None) – Optional high-symmetry points in fractional reciprocal coordinates. When omitted, ASE derives them from the primitive cell.

  • labels_path – Optional band path as a sequence of label paths, e.g. [['N', 'G', 'H', 'P', 'G']].

  • formula (str | None) – Optional label used in the output filename and plot title.

  • info (dict | None) – Optional metadata dictionary; if it contains label or title, that value is used in the plot title.

  • supercell_matrix – Optional Phonopy supercell matrix. When omitted, a 3x3x3 diagonal supercell is used.

  • primitive_matrix – Primitive-cell setting passed to Phonopy. The default "auto" keeps the standard primitive-cell phonon workflow for crystals like BCC while silencing the corresponding Phonopy default warning.

Returns:

Path to the saved phonon-dispersion figure.

Return type:

str

Raises:

  • ImportError – If the required phonopy or spglib dependency is missing.

  • RuntimeError – If the primitive cell cannot be determined from structure.

Serialize calculated basic-property results to a JSON summary file.

  • Cij (array-like) – Elastic constants array.

  • surface_energy (array-like) – Surface energies ordered by miller_indices_list.

  • vacancy_formation_energy (float) – Point-defect formation energies in eV.

  • octahedral_formation_energy (float) – Point-defect formation energies in eV.

  • tetrahedral_formation_energy (float) – Point-defect formation energies in eV.

  • inter_100_formation_energy (float) – Dumbbell/interstitial formation energies in eV.

  • inter_110_formation_energy (float) – Dumbbell/interstitial formation energies in eV.

  • inter_111_formation_energy (float) – Dumbbell/interstitial formation energies in eV.

  • miller_indices_list (list[tuple[int, int, int]] | None) – Miller indices associated with surface_energy.

  • save_name (str) – Output JSON filename saved inside self.working_dir.

  • volume_scale (float) – Divisors applied before serialization, matching the historical script output.

  • energy_scale (float) – Divisors applied before serialization, matching the historical script output.

Returns:

Path to the saved JSON file.

Return type:

str

Build, relax, and plot generalized stacking-fault energy curves.

stacking_fault(a, b, miller, distance, layers=18, num_steps=10, fmax=0.01, steps=1000, write_xyz=True)

Calculate a generalized stacking-fault energy curve.

Parameters:

  • a (sequence[float]) – In-plane slab vectors in scaled coordinates passed to ase.build.cut.

  • b (sequence[float]) – In-plane slab vectors in scaled coordinates passed to ase.build.cut.

  • miller (sequence[int]) – Miller-index label used in filenames and summary output.

  • distance (float) – Fractional translation distance applied along vector a.

  • layers (int) – Number of layers in the generated slab.

  • num_steps (int) – Number of sliding increments along the reaction path.

  • fmax (float) – Force threshold used during each relaxation.

  • steps (int) – Maximum optimizer steps for each relaxation.

  • write_xyz (bool) – Whether to write each relaxed shifted slab to an XYZ trajectory.

Returns:

Stacking-fault energies in eV/Angstrom^2 relative to the unshifted slab.

Return type:

list[float]
